guidance: Even-strength shot-share arithmetic from counts you already have. It describes what happened, not what will: Corsi ignores shot quality, and a single game's PDO is mostly noise that tends back toward 100.
method: All counts are at even strength. Corsi For is shots on goal plus missed shots plus blocked attempts, and Corsi Against adds the same three counts for the opponent; Corsi For % is 100 x CF / (CF + CA), so 50 % is an even share. Fenwick drops the blocked attempts (the NHL calls it unblocked shot attempts), so FF = shots + misses and FF% divides those totals the same way. Shooting percentage is 100 x goals for / shots on goal for; save percentage is 100 x (shots against - goals against) / shots against; PDO is the two added together, matching the NHL's SPSV%, and 100 is break-even. Goals cannot exceed shots on goal because every goal is also a shot on goal, and a zero shot count is refused because the corresponding percentage has no denominator. Counts are whole numbers from 0 to 500 per side, percentages are rounded to one decimal, a total under 20 attempts carries a small-sample warning, and a PDO five points or more from 100 carries a regression warning. The figures are descriptive: Corsi approximates possession without weighing shot location or quality, PDO in a single game is mostly noise, and nothing is adjusted for score effects, zone starts or special teams.

sources.title: Corsi (statistic) - shot attempts are shots on goal plus blocked and missed attempts, and Corsi For % is CF / (CF + CA)
Fenwick (statistic) - unblocked shot attempts (USAT) keep shots on goal and missed shots but exclude blocked attempts
Analytics in ice hockey - PDO is a team's shooting percentage plus its save percentage multiplied by 100, called SPSV% by the NHL
